translations.source_sense_description: Blüten aufweisen

glosses: Produire des fleurs, se couvrir de fleurs, ou être en fleurs.

examples.text: Mon Dieu, mon Dieu ! quand on vient des pays où fleurit l’oranger, où trillent les cigales saoulées de soleil, comment se plaire ici ?
C’était un soir de mai. Les marronniers venaient de fleurir devant la mairie. On guettait les asperges dans les jardins.
Mais, au jour du revoir, une porte s’ouvre et l’enclos renaît et le tulipier fleurit, même au cœur du plus âpre hiver.

glosses: Être dans un état de prospérité, de splendeur ; être en crédit, en honneur, en réputation.

examples.text: Dans un siècle où fleurissent les arts.
Les peintres et les poètes qui fleurissent à cette époque.
Les sciences et les beaux-arts fleurissaient.

glosses: Se développer, apparaître.

examples.text: Il se gratte le front qu’un prurit tenace ne cesse de taquiner, et où fleurissent des taches rougeâtres.
Joseph le vit disparaître avec une certaine irritation et il le jugea un peu dur, malgré ce sourire de pasteur qui fleurissait à tout moment sur sa bouche.

Et si, aujourd’hui, il devient possible de tendre la perche, ce n’est pas comme une invitation à l’échange, au dialogue ou au débat d’idées… C’est un selfie stick uniquement destiné à prendre un reflet de soi-même qui fleurit sur les lieux touristiques.
[Les grelots] ont d’abord chanté dans mon cœur, puis ils ont fleuri à mon chaperon

glosses: Parer d’une fleur, d’un bouquet.

examples.text: Qui vous a fleuri de la sorte ? — Cette année, on ne fleurira pas la tombe du soldat inconnu.
Agenouillées, elles fleurissent de nouvelles fleurs son piédestal moussu.

glosses: Orner.

examples.text: Les Palmes académiques, dont le Quatorze Juillet va fleurir tant de boutonnières, m'ont laissé toute une suite d'impressions désastreuses.

glosses: Prendre des fleurs pour en faire un bouquet ou pour s’en parer.

examples.text: – Madame, Monsieur, en voulez-vous de nos belles violettes, de nos jonquilles ? C’est deux sous. Fleurissez-vous ! Fleurissez-vous !

translations.source_sense_description: Wirtschaft, Handel: sehr gut laufen, sich wirtschaftlich gut entwickeln

glosses: To thrive or grow well.

examples.text: The barley flourished in the warm weather.

'Twas early June, the new grass was flourishing everywheres, the posies in the yard—peonies and such—in full bloom, the sun was shining, and the water of the bay was blue, with light green streaks where the shoal showed.

glosses: To prosper or fare well.

examples.text: The town flourished with the coming of the railway.
The cooperation flourished as the customers rushed in the business.
Bad men as frequently prosper and flourish, and that by the means of their wickedness.
One hall called Civil Law Hall or School, flouriſhed about this time (though in its buildings decayed) by the care of the learned and judicious Dr. Will. Warham Principal or Moderator thereof […]

glosses: To be in a period of greatest influence.

examples.text: His writing flourished before the war.

glosses: To develop; to make thrive; to expand.

examples.text: But all that I ſhall ſay in this vvhole Argument, vvill be but like Bottomes of Thred, cloſe vvound vp, vvhich vvith a good Needle (perhaps) may be flouriſhed into large VVorkes.

glosses: To make bold, sweeping movements with.

examples.text: They flourished the banner as they stormed the palace.
The squirrel flourished its fluffy tail about as an alarm signal after its narrow escape from the cat.

glosses: To make bold and sweeping, fanciful, or wanton movements, by way of ornament, parade, bravado, etc.; to play with fantastic and irregular motion.

examples.text: Impetuous spread the stream, and smoking flourished o'er his head.

glosses: To use florid language; to indulge in rhetorical figures and lofty expressions.

examples.text: They dilate […] and flourish long upon little incidents.

glosses: To make ornamental strokes with the pen; to write graceful, decorative figures.
To adorn with beautiful figures or rhetoric; to ornament with anything showy; to embellish.

examples.text:
With shadowy verdure flourish'd high,
A sudden youth the groves enjoy.
To bring you thus together, 'tis no sin, Sith that the justice of your title to him Doth flourish the deceit.

glosses: To execute an irregular or fanciful strain of music, by way of ornament or prelude.

examples.text: Why do the emperor's trumpets flourish thus?

glosses: To boast; to vaunt; to brag.
To brandish (a weapon).
A dramatic gesture such as the waving of a flag.

examples.text: With many flourishes of the captured banner, they marched down the avenue.
This is my substitute for pistol and ball. With a philosophical flourish Cato throws himself upon his sword; I quietly take to the ship.
Gabriel Jesus' solo goal - as a stunned United pushed for an equaliser - was a flourish that eased any late nerves.

glosses: An ornamentation.

examples.text: His signature ended with a flourish.

[B]revity is the soul of wit,
And tediousness the limbs and outward flourishes[.]

glosses: A ceremonious passage such as a fanfare.

examples.text: The trumpets blew a flourish as they entered the church.
[I]f he is a soldier in command, successes will be amplified, and the results of his campaigns announced with a flourish of trumpets.

glosses: A decorative embellishment on a building.

translations.source_sense_description: Wirtschaft, Handel: sehr gut laufen, sich wirtschaftlich gut entwickeln

glosses: To grow or increase stature; to grow vigorously or luxuriantly, to flourish.

examples.text: Not all animals thrive well in captivity.
to thrive upon hard work
